helpIntro: UC Berkeley uses a 4.0 scale. Enter semester units and final grades; A+ and A are 4.0, plus/minus grades use Berkeley values, F counts as 0.0, and P/NP is excluded from GPA.
helpNote: For standard undergraduate Berkeley GPA planning. Repeat Impact is disabled because Berkeley replacement depends on your cumulative repeat-unit history: the first 12 graded repeat units generally use the second grade, while later repeats count both attempts. Graduate GPA rules are separate.
helpExample: A 4-unit A earns 16.0 grade points and a 4-unit B+ earns 13.2. Together, 29.2 ÷ 8 = 3.650.

gradeExplanations.A+: A+ earns 4.0 grade points per unit, the same as A.
gradeExplanations.F: F earns 0.0 points; its units are included in GPA computation.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete; excluded from GPA for assignments from fall 1973 onward until resolved.
gradeExplanations.IP: In Progress; excluded until a final grade is assigned.
gradeExplanations.NR: Not Reported; temporary administrative grade excluded from GPA.
gradeExplanations.M: Missing; temporary administrative grade excluded from GPA.

specialTypes.name: UC Berkeley course
specialTypes.note: Use final Berkeley letter grades and semester units; P/NP and temporary marks follow the grade table.

specialTypes.name: Other UC campus course that transfers grade points
specialTypes.note: Other UC campus grades can enter the Berkeley GPA when posted as grade-point transfer work. Confirm the Transfer Credit Report.

specialTypes.name: UC Berkeley Extension XB after matriculation
specialTypes.note: XB courses completed after matriculation can enter the Berkeley GPA. Confirm the Transfer Credit Report.

specialTypes.name: Non-UC / ordinary external transfer credit
specialTypes.note: Ordinary transfer grades from non-UC institutions generally do not enter the Berkeley GPA.

repeatPolicy.note: Repeat Impact is disabled. Berkeley generally replaces the first grade with the second for the first 12 graded repeat units; beyond that threshold both grades count. Use your official record or adviser to determine which attempts are in your GPA.
